title: Loose Parts Trolley
strapline: A trolley of corks, rings, reels and pebbles that rolls anywhere and becomes anything the child needs.
intent: Children think symbolically — a cork is a cake, a coin or a candle, and the child decides.
Children sort, classify and pattern by their own rules, and can tell you the rule.
Children feed transporting, positioning and enclosing schemas with materials made to be moved.
Children count, compare and subitise with objects that matter to them in the moment.
Children own the outcome completely — there is no wrong way to arrange a tray of shells.
implementation: Stock a mobile trolley with sorted, sectioned collections so it can roll to wherever the play is happening.
Keep every choice visible — open tins, clear jars, tinker trays — so children can see the whole palette at a glance.
Resist naming what a thing 'is' — follow the child's meaning and let a curtain ring be a steering wheel all morning.
Add tools that up the precision — tweezers, tongs, scoops, muffin tins and empty frames to arrange inside.
Spot schemas and feed them: the child filling a bag with pebbles and carrying them off is working hard.
Photograph favourite arrangements before tidy-up, and add mirrors and frames to dignify them as art.
Restock from local walks so the collection keeps its story — conkers in autumn, blossom in spring.
key_questions: I wonder why you put all of those ones together?
What could this be in your game?
What comes next in your pattern?
Have we got enough rings to go all the way round the edge?
Where else could that one go — have you tried it?

impact.text: Children sort and group by their own logic and defend their categories.
Children copy, continue and create patterns along edges and rims and predict what comes next.
Children subitise small handfuls that land in a tray — 'three!' — without counting.
Loose parts stand in for anything in pretend play, and children narrate the game as they go.
Children choose and combine materials their own way and own the result with pride.
Small hands grow precise — tweezers lift a single sequin, a ring threads onto a stick.
Children carry, fill, empty and arrange, feeding transporting and positioning schemas.

enhancements: Tweezers, tongs and tiny bowls to turn arranging into a precision workout.
Muffin tins, ice-cube trays and egg boxes that quietly invite one-in-each-space counting.
Empty picture frames and mirror tiles as stages for transient art.
A basket of curtain rings and dowels for threading, stacking and spinning.
Story stones or a favourite book beside the trolley to spark small-world play.
Labelled tins so children sort and return the parts themselves at tidy-up.
A 'treasure of the week' from a local walk to refresh the collection.

playing_exploring: The same trolley becomes a shop, a kitchen and a rocket in one week.
Children explore with all their senses — weight, shine, sound and texture all inform the choosing.
active_learning: With no finished picture to match, children set their own goals and decide when it's done.
creating_thinking: One object standing for another is early abstract thinking — the root of symbols, letters and numbers.
Children carry an idea from one collection to the next — what worked on the plate rim gets tried on the shelf.
